title: How email works
examples: What is the difference between a server and a computer?
How does the internet know where to send my email?
Can you explain what an email protocol is?

explain.say: When you send an email, it does not go straight to your friend's inbox.
Your email address must follow a specific format to work correctly.
Protocols are like rules that let different computers talk to each other.
Mail servers are powerful computers that store and manage emails.
Spam filters are programs that check emails for unwanted junk content.
In real life, when you use a school network, the server manages all your class files.

faq.q: If I send an email, does it go through the physical internet cables?
faq.a: Yes, the data travels as electrical signals through cables connected to servers. It is not magic; it follows established pathways.
asks: How does data move across the internet?

faq.q: What happens if my email address has a typo?
faq.a: The sending server will usually send a bounce-back message back to you. This tells you that the address was incorrect.
asks: How do I know if my email address is wrong?

faq.q: Are protocols different for sending and receiving mail?
faq.a: Yes, sending uses protocols like SMTP, while receiving often uses POP3 or IMAP. These are different sets of rules.
asks: What is the difference between POP and IMAP?
Do I need different rules for sending and reading?

faq.q: How do spam filters know what is junk mail?
faq.a: They use complex rules and learning algorithms to look for patterns common in spam. They are constantly updated to catch new types.

faq.q: Does the recipient's computer need to be on for the email to arrive?
faq.a: No, the email first lands on the recipient's mail server. It waits there until the recipient's device connects to the internet.
asks: Can I send an email if they are offline?
Where does it wait if they are not using email?

facts: The structure user@domain.com is the standard email format.
SMTP is the protocol primarily used to send emails across the internet.
Mail servers act as post offices for electronic mail.
Spam filters analyze message content and sender reputation.

quiz.say: If you send an email to someone whose domain name is wrong, what will likely happen?

options.show: It will wait until the recipient calls you.
options.say: It will wait until the recipient calls you.

options.show: It will automatically correct the address.
options.say: It will automatically correct the address.

quiz.why: The sending server will detect the invalid address and send an error message back to you.

wrong.0: This is incorrect; email delivery is automated by servers, not by phone calls.
wrong.2: This is tempting because it sounds like the message vanished, but the server usually sends an error.
wrong.3: This is wrong because email systems do not have spell-check for entire domains.

quiz.say: Which component is mainly responsible for receiving and holding incoming mail?
quiz.why: The mail server is the digital post office that accepts and stores your messages until you check them.

wrong.0: The filter only checks; the server is the main storage location.
wrong.2: Your computer only reads mail; the server is where it is stored first.
wrong.3: The cable only carries the signal; the server handles the actual storage.

quiz.say: If you want to check your email on your phone and your laptop, which protocol helps keep them synced?
quiz.why: IMAP keeps your emails synchronized across multiple devices so you see the same thing everywhere.

wrong.0: SMTP is only for sending mail, not for viewing copies on different devices.
wrong.1: POP3 usually downloads and deletes mail from the server, causing sync issues.
wrong.2: The domain system only finds the server; it does not manage the message synchronization.
